title: review: LS2b: the auto-handover section ends at an explicit marker and renders titles on one line; the plan size nag ignores that section
spec:
Bug in LS2 (on goal/T-1590): handover.write() ends the old section at the next line starting with '## ' (orchestrator/handover.py ~line 301). But _render_section embeds titles verbatim (`### {goal['id']} {goal['title']}` in _goal_lines ~line 109, and _task_ref), and goal T-1391's title contains '\n\n## Evidence\n- In luna-inbox, t'. The section is cut at that embedded heading; the rest of the old render is kept as 'tail' and the new render is written before it, so plan.md grows by one copy on every write. Separately, the daemon's render is about 12k chars today (open goals list all children), so the LS1 plan-size nag (planner_context.py, plan_max_chars 12000) would fire on the daemon's own output.

1. Rendering: every title interpolated into the section (goal headings in _goal_lines, _task_ref, any other) is collapsed to one line (whitespace runs including newlines become one space) and capped at 160 chars with a trailing '…' when cut. No rendered line inside the section may start with '## ' except the section heading.
2. Boundary: _render_section ends the section with the line `<!-- end auto-handover -->`. write() takes the old section from the last '## Auto-handover ' heading through that marker line (inclusive) when the marker follows the heading; the tail is what follows the marker. Without the marker (legacy section), the old section runs to EOF. Remove the next-'## '-heading rule. Keep the last-heading rule, temp-file plus os.replace, the snapshot-hash short-circuit and the section == old_section no-op.
3. orchestrator/planner_context.py: the plan_max_chars check measures plan.md with the auto-handover section (heading through marker, or through EOF without a marker) removed.
acceptance:
tests/test_handover.py::test_write_with_multiline_goal_title_does_not_grow passes: a goal whose title contains '

## Evidence
x' is rendered on one line; three write() calls with changing bus state leave exactly one Auto-handover heading, one end marker and no '## Evidence' line in plan.md

tests/test_handover.py::test_write_keeps_sections_after_marker passes: plan.md with '## A', a marker-terminated Auto-handover section, then '## B' keeps '## B' and its body byte-for-byte after write()
tests/test_handover.py::test_write_legacy_section_without_marker_runs_to_eof passes: a section without the marker is replaced through EOF
tests/test_planner_context.py::test_plan_size_nag_ignores_auto_handover passes: plan.md whose own text is under plan_max_chars but whose auto-handover section pushes it over returns no nag
tests/test_handover.py::test_write_keeps_sections_after_handover and tests/test_planner_context.py::test_plan_size_nag still pass (fixtures may move to the marker form)

result.summary: The marker boundary, the last-heading rule and the planner_context change look right. The title collapse is incomplete: other task-supplied text is still rendered raw, so a multi-line value can still break the section. I did not run the tests.

comments.issue: Spec item 1 requires every interpolated title or free text to be collapsed to one line. Only `title` goes through `_title`. `t['reason']` (failed group, line ~134), `hold_reason` (line ~127), `executor` (line ~122), and `e['task']` and `e['kind']` in the events tail (line ~249) are still interpolated raw. A failed task whose reason contains '\n## Foo' or '\n<!-- end auto-handover -->' puts a '## ' line, or a fake end marker, inside the section. That brings back the same growth bug through a different field. Pass these values through a one-line sanitizer.

The multiline-title test covers only the title field. No test covers newline-bearing reason, hold_reason or event text. It also does not check that no rendered line other than the heading starts with '## ', which spec item 1 requires.
